open_points.subject: compose-and-prove flow: missing referenced records
open_points.text: A16 rule 1: "A request naming a record that does not exist ... is refused as State 0's unknown reference before that record's own checks, never as a proof failure" vs A05 rule 1 phase 1: "a function node names an existing contract version; an operation node names a binding in status `accepted`" and A05 rule 7: "Composition keeps any other flow version whether or not it is proven."
open_points.question: If a composed flow version references a non-existent contract version or binding, must composition be refused as unknown reference (and keep nothing), or must the version be kept and marked unproven by proof phase 1?
options: Refuse composition as unknown reference before keeping a version
Keep the version and return an unproven proof result naming the missing node reference
open_points.default_guess: Keep the version and return proof failure (to preserve State 0 'kept either way' behavior).

open_points.subject: file media-type equality in proof and wiring
open_points.text: A05 phase 3 requires ports to carry "the same media type (K-06)", but no canonical comparison rule is defined for media types.
open_points.question: How is media-type equality decided (exact string, case-insensitive type/subtype, parameter handling, whitespace normalization)?
options: RFC-style media type comparison (case-insensitive type/subtype, normalized parameters)
Case-insensitive on full token, parameters must match exactly

open_points.subject: HTTP required header name collisions with kernel-set headers
open_points.text: A09 rule 1 says sent headers are exactly `host`, `accept-encoding: identity`, required headers, credential header, and body headers; only duplicate required headers and credential-vs-required collision are explicitly refused.
open_points.question: What happens if `required_headers` contains `host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, or `content-length` (case-insensitive): refuse, override kernel values, or send duplicates?
options: Refuse binding/proposal as manifest mismatch on reserved-header collision
Send both values as duplicate headers
open_points.default_guess: Refuse on any collision with kernel-managed header names.

open_points.subject: surface request byte-size limit measurement
open_points.text: A16 rule 1: request size is "counted as the bytes of the request message as received" and must be within `surface_request_bytes_max`.
open_points.question: What exact byte sequence is measured for the limit under MCP transport (parsed payload only, full frame, or transport-level bytes)?
options: Count only the decoded request payload bytes (post-framing)
Count full MCP frame bytes as received on the socket
Count transport bytes after any compression/encoding decoding
open_points.default_guess: Count full MCP frame bytes as received by the kernel listener.
